title: What Do Plants Need? A Parent Guide
endLine: Green plants need light and water to make food.

scenes.tts: Does a plant really need sunlight if it already has water? Four cups of radish seedlings and a dark cupboard give a fair answer.
scenes.caption: Does a plant really need sunlight if it already has water? Four cups of radish seedlings and a dark cupboard give a fair answer.
scenes.visual: Friendly schematic windowsill with soft daylight. A paper cup of small green radish seedlings sits on the sill, filling much of the frame; beside it, a cupboard door stands slightly open, dark inside. Large high-contrast question text: 'Water, but no light?' Leaves sway gently. No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: Does a plant really need sunlight if it already has water? Four cups of radish seedlings and a dark cupboard give a fair answer.

scenes.visual: Same windowsill and cupboard. Title 'What Do Plants Need?' appears above for two seconds.

scenes.tts: Setup takes about thirty minutes, then quick checks every day or two for about two weeks. Your child practices running a fair test. They make a guess, change one thing, and check the result over time.
scenes.caption: Setup takes about thirty minutes, then quick checks every day or two for about two weeks. Your child practices running a fair test. They make a guess, change one thing, and check the result over time.
scenes.visual: Four cups appear in a row on a tray. Three labels appear one by one with small icons: 'Guess, then check' (pencil), 'Change one thing' (a single highlighted cup), 'Watch over time' (calendar with ticks).
scenes.narration: Setup takes about thirty minutes, then quick checks every day or two for about two weeks. Your child practices running a fair test. They make a guess, change one thing, and check the result over time.

scenes.tts: You need four small cups, with holes an adult pokes in the bottom. Add a tray, potting mix, and radish seeds. Bring water, a tablespoon, labels, and a cupboard or a big box for a dark place.
scenes.caption: You need four small cups, with holes an adult pokes in the bottom. Add a tray, potting mix, and radish seeds. Bring water, a tablespoon, labels, and a cupboard or a big box for a dark place.
scenes.visual: Items settle around the tray: four paper cups with an adult hand poking small holes in one bottom, a bag of potting mix, a radish seed packet, a cup of water with a tablespoon, masking tape and marker, and an upturned cardboard box.
scenes.narration: You need four small cups, with holes an adult pokes in the bottom. Add a tray, potting mix, and radish seeds. Bring water, a tablespoon, labels, and a cupboard or a big box for a dark place.

scenes.tts: Have an adult open the potting mix with scissors outdoors or by an open window. Keep your child back and turn your face away. Dampen the mix before scooping to reduce dust. Read the seed packet and choose untreated seeds.
scenes.caption: Have an adult open the potting mix with scissors outdoors or by an open window. Keep your child back and turn your face away. Dampen the mix before scooping to reduce dust. Read the seed packet and choose untreated seeds.
scenes.visual: By the same window, show the adult turning their face away and opening the bag with scissors. Keep the child outside the work area. Show water darkening the mix, then bring the seed packet into view and highlight its untreated label.
scenes.narration: Have an adult open the potting mix with scissors outdoors or by an open window. Keep your child back and turn your face away. Dampen the mix before scooping to reduce dust. Read the seed packet and choose untreated seeds.

scenes.tts: Fill the four cups and label them: light plus water, dark plus water, light no water, dark no water. Your child presses four or five seeds into each cup and covers them. Give each cup two tablespoons of water.
scenes.caption: Fill the four cups and label them: light plus water, dark plus water, light no water, dark no water. Your child presses four or five seeds into each cup and covers them. Give each cup two tablespoons of water.
scenes.visual: The four cups fill with dark damp mix. Tape labels appear on each: 'light + water', 'dark + water', 'light, no water', 'dark, no water'. Small seeds press in and are covered; a tablespoon of water pours into each cup twice.
scenes.narration: Fill the four cups and label them: light plus water, dark plus water, light no water, dark no water. Your child presses four or five seeds into each cup and covers them. Give each cup two tablespoons of water.

scenes.tts: Keep all four cups on a sunny windowsill. When the top feels dry, water each cup the same amount. Sprouts usually appear in three to ten days. When most seedlings are about two centimeters tall, have your child predict what will happen to each cup. Write or draw their guesses.
scenes.caption: Keep all four cups on a sunny windowsill. When the top feels dry, water each cup the same amount. Sprouts usually appear in three to ten days. When most seedlings are about two centimeters tall, have your child predict what will happen to each cup. Write or draw their guesses.
scenes.visual: Keep all four cups on the sunny windowsill. Give each the same water. Show most sprouts reaching a height marker labeled "About 2 cm". Show the adult recording the child’s guesses beside the cup labels and saving the sheet for the last scene.
scenes.narration: Keep all four cups on a sunny windowsill. When the top feels dry, water each cup the same amount. Sprouts usually appear in three to ten days. When most seedlings are about two centimeters tall, have your child predict what will happen to each cup. Write or draw their guesses.

scenes.tts: Use a cupboard free of cleaners that children cannot climb into. Move both dark cups inside and shut the door. Give each water cup two tablespoons when the top feels dry. Stop watering the other cups. Compare cups that differ only in light, or only in water.
scenes.caption: Use a cupboard free of cleaners that children cannot climb into. Move both dark cups inside and shut the door. Give each water cup two tablespoons when the top feels dry. Stop watering the other cups. Compare cups that differ only in light, or only in water.
scenes.visual: Carry the two dark cups from the windowsill into a cupboard with empty shelves apart from the cups. An adult closes the door fully. Show two spoonfuls going only to each watered cup when its surface is dry. Highlight the two watered cups, then the two windowsill cups.
scenes.narration: Use a cupboard free of cleaners that children cannot climb into. Move both dark cups inside and shut the door. Give each water cup two tablespoons when the top feels dry. Stop watering the other cups. Compare cups that differ only in light, or only in water.

scenes.tts: Picture the two cups that still get water. After about a week, how might the dark seedlings compare with the windowsill seedlings? Shorter, the same height, or taller?
scenes.caption: Picture the two cups that still get water. After about a week, how might the dark seedlings compare with the windowsill seedlings? Shorter, the same height, or taller?
scenes.visual: Split frame: the windowsill 'light + water' cup on the left, the cupboard 'dark + water' cup on the right with its seedlings hidden by a soft question mark. A high-contrast question card: 'Shorter, same, or taller?'
scenes.narration: Picture the two cups that still get water. After about a week, how might the dark seedlings compare with the windowsill seedlings? Shorter, the same height, or taller?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card and the split frame. Leaves in the light cup sway slightly; a soft ring turns beneath the question. No answer shown.

scenes.tts: The dark seedlings are often taller, thinner, and paler. They may lean or flop as they stretch on stored food. When you compare your cups, ask, 'What do you notice besides height?'
scenes.caption: The dark seedlings are often taller, thinner, and paler. They may lean or flop as they stretch on stored food. When you compare your cups, ask, 'What do you notice besides height?'
scenes.visual: Lift the question mark to show one typical result. The dark seedlings are tall, pale, and leaning. The light seedlings are green and upright. Use the label "What you may see" and keep both cups visible for comparison.
scenes.narration: The dark seedlings are often taller, thinner, and paler. They may lean or flop as they stretch on stored food. When you compare your cups, ask, 'What do you notice besides height?'

scenes.tts: Every day or two, take a quick look and return the dark cups. Draw each cup. Note height, color, and drooping. The dry cups usually droop within two to five days. Dark seedlings weaken over one to two weeks. The light and water cup stays green and upright.
scenes.caption: Every day or two, take a quick look and return the dark cups. Draw each cup. Note height, color, and drooping. The dry cups usually droop within two to five days. Dark seedlings weaken over one to two weeks. The light and water cup stays green and upright.
scenes.visual: An adult opens the cupboard for a quick look, returns the dark cups, and shuts the door. Add quick drawings to the observation sheet, then show the dry cups drooping, the dark watered cup weakening, and the light watered cup staying upright.
scenes.narration: Every day or two, take a quick look and return the dark cups. Draw each cup. Note height, color, and drooping. The dry cups usually droop within two to five days. Dark seedlings weaken over one to two weeks. The light and water cup stays green and upright.

scenes.tts: A green plant makes its own food in its leaves. It uses light, water, and a gas from the air. In the dark, a seedling lives on stored food. When that runs out, it cannot make more.
scenes.caption: A green plant makes its own food in its leaves. It uses light, water, and a gas from the air. In the dark, a seedling lives on stored food. When that runs out, it cannot make more.
scenes.visual: Zoom into a leaf on the same windowsill seedling. Show light, water, and a labeled air input reaching the leaf as a schematic sugar icon forms. Pull back to the dark seedling and let its stored-food indicator drain.
scenes.narration: A green plant makes its own food in its leaves. It uses light, water, and a gas from the air. In the dark, a seedling lives on stored food. When that runs out, it cannot make more.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child while they plant and water. Nobody tastes the seeds, soil, or plants. Keep seeds and marker caps away from children under four. If a child is choking, call nine one one. Wash hands with soap and water after planting and after each check.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child while they plant and water. Nobody tastes the seeds, soil, or plants. Keep seeds and marker caps away from children under four. If a child is choking, call nine one one. Wash hands with soap and water after planting and after each check.
scenes.visual: Beside the same tray, show an adult staying with the child. Cross out tasting seeds, soil, and sprouts together. Show seeds and a marker cap stored out of reach with the warning "Under 4: choking risk". Then show hands being washed with soap and water. Use "Call 911" for the emergency line.
scenes.narration: Stay with your child while they plant and water. Nobody tastes the seeds, soil, or plants. Keep seeds and marker caps away from children under four. If a child is choking, call nine one one. Wash hands with soap and water after planting and after each check.

scenes.tts: At the end, lay the first guesses beside the cups. Ask, 'What surprised you?' Then ask, 'Where does a green plant get its food?' Let your child point to a cup as they explain.
scenes.caption: At the end, lay the first guesses beside the cups. Ask, 'What surprised you?' Then ask, 'Where does a green plant get its food?' Let your child point to a cup as they explain.
scenes.visual: Bring the guess sheet back beside the four cups. An illustrated hand points to a seedling while the two debrief questions appear in turn.
scenes.narration: At the end, lay the first guesses beside the cups. Ask, 'What surprised you?' Then ask, 'Where does a green plant get its food?' Let your child point to a cup as they explain.

scenes.line: Green plants need light and water to make food.
scenes.visual: End card with the green 'light + water' cup faint in the background. Centered, large, high-contrast text: 'Green plants need light and water to make food.'
